title: Goal Setting for Growth

sections.markdown:
Setting goals is one of the best ways you can improve personal readiness, professional development, and long-term success. Whether the objective is improving financial health, advancing a career, strengthening relationships, or increasing physical fitness, a clear plan helps turn intentions into action.

The [Marine Corps Total Fitness (MCTF)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/news/unlocking-total-fitnes-essential-resources-for-marines-and-their-families) framework encourages Marines to view readiness as more than physical performance. Financial stability, mental fitness, social connections, spiritual well-being, and career development all contribute to mission readiness. Because these areas are connected, progress in one often strengthens another. For example, paying down debt can improve financial security, reduce stress, strengthen family relationships, and increase focus on the mission.

The [Personal Readiness Seminar (PRS)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/pfmp) helps Marines establish a strong foundation early in their careers by providing practical information about financial readiness, education, career development, relationships, military resources, and personal responsibility. Marines can use these resources to create a spending plan, build an emergency fund, complete professional military education, earn a credential, or identify a mentor who supports their long-term goals.

The Financial Education Action Points (FEAPs) reinforce financial readiness during major life and career milestones, including a permanent change of station (PCS), deployment, marriage, the birth of a child, continuation pay, and transition from military service. These events provide valuable opportunities to reassess goals, identify potential financial risks, and make informed decisions before challenges become emergencies.

sections.heading: Effective goals should be:
sections.markdown:
- **S**pecific – Clearly define what you want to accomplish.
- **M**easurable – Track progress using numbers or milestones.
- **A**chievable – Set realistic goals based on available resources.
- **R**elevant – Align goals with your personal values, career, or readiness priorities.
- **T**ime-bound – Establish a deadline to stay accountable.

For example, instead of saying, "I want to save more money," a SMART goal would be: "I will save $150 from each paycheck until I build a $1,500 emergency fund."

Successful goal setting also includes identifying action steps, anticipating obstacles, using available resources, and reviewing progress regularly. Marines don't have to accomplish their goals alone. Leaders, mentors, command financial specialists, [personal financial managers](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/pfmp), education professionals, career planners, and installation support programs can all provide guidance along the way.

Setting SMART goals does more than produce measurable results. It builds discipline, confidence, resilience, and decision-making skills that support both military performance and everyday life. By breaking larger goals into clear, achievable steps, SMART objectives can also help reduce stress during challenging or uncertain periods by providing structure, focus, and a sense of progress. By using Marine Corps Total Fitness, the Personal Readiness Seminar, and Financial Education Action Points as part of the goal-setting process, Marines strengthen their readiness today while preparing for future success.
